fixtures.label: Every open receivable, aged by due date
fixtures.description:
The PRIMARY document — the whole receivable book on the route's default anchor (`due_date`, the one the live Xero tenant ages by), and the only fixture whose Account column spans UNRELATED customers. Address `all:-:due_date`. Re-captured 2026-09-09: 29 open receivables grouping to 16 accounts, $47,298.03. ⚠️ An `all` run is a fact about the DAY it ran — re-measure those three numbers on every re-capture rather than carrying them.

Three jobs. (1) THE UNTRIMMED CHAIN. `statement.eta` trims each line's chain against its own scope; this family prints the whole chain on every row, and an `all` run is where that matters most — no common prefix to trim against, no addressee to have already named it. Censused 2026-09-07 over all 318 prod orgs, the 29 department nodes carry 8 distinct names, 24 sharing `Locations`, `Office` and `Transpo`, so two accounts can both be a `Locations` separated only by the levels a leaf segment discards (api-cloudrun#923).

(2) THE `all` SCOPE LINE — "Every open receivable", with `organization_path` `null`; the arm neither sibling reaches. ⭐ That null says something about the RUN ("not about one account") rather than about an account, which is why core#92 could replace the old `scope.name: ""` with it.

(3) A NOT-YET-DUE ROW — forward-dated invoices land in `current` with a NEGATIVE days-overdue, the case behind the defect where a right-aligned Days column ran into the Bucket and printed `-17Current` as one number.

⚠️ 31-60, 61-90 and 90+ read $0.00 on EVERY fixture here — nothing in the book is that old; only an `all:-:date` run reaches 31-60, and a bucket column is a value rather than a branch, so that earned no fourth capture.

⭐ THIS GOLDEN IS WHERE core#91 IS VISIBLE, and checkably so: 16 accounts render under 16 DISTINCT labels, and the matrix and the detail name each account identically. Before it, fakes were drawn per FIELD PATH — 14 accounts under 10 labels, two rows both reading `Foxglove Films LLC` at $8,350.00 and $49.92.

fixtures.label: Scoped to a subtree, aged by invoice date
fixtures.description:
The only SCOPED run, the only "and N sub-accounts" sentence, and the only fixture on the `date` anchor — three arms `all-accounts` cannot reach. Address `organization-subtree:gql6Tjro2tSVrgP5NKOH:date` — the widest prod org family at 14 nodes, the root behind the statement family's `balance-forward-subtree`. Re-captured 2026-09-09: 3 invoices across 2 accounts, $2,650.52.

(1) THE SCOPE LINE'S OTHER ARM. `scope.kind === "organization"`, so the heading composes `organization_path` (core#92 replaced the stored `scope.name` with the chain) and, because `uids.length` is 14, appends "and 13 sub-accounts" — the plural branch of a sentence that is singular at 2 and absent at 1. `nothing-outstanding` holds the absent arm.

(2) THE ANCHOR, AND IT IS NOT COSMETIC — measured on this fixture's own three invoices. Aged by `date` the page reads current $1,135.57 / 1-30 $1,514.95; aged by `due_date` all three fall due after the as-of and the whole $2,650.52 is `current`. One account is either wholly current or more than half overdue depending on which stored date you age from — which is why the document states which it used, and why `anchorText` prints "Invoice date" here against "Due date" on both siblings. (⭐ That $1,514.95 is invoices 2402 + 2403, the figure `balance-forward-subtree` ties to the live Xero tenant through a different fold.)

⚠️ `buildAgingReport` REFUSES any as-of but today's Chicago date, so a re-capture renders different money BY CONSTRUCTION. Re-measure rather than carry — these figures survived 2026-09-08 → 09 unchanged, which is luck, not a guarantee.

(3) TWO ACCOUNTS SHARING A PREFIX, so the untrimmed chain is exercised exactly where `statement.eta` would have trimmed it away. ⚠️ Deliberately SMALL, so the anchor is the only thing worth looking at in the diff.

⭐ The two tables now name the same account the SAME way — core#91 seeds on the organization's identity, not the field path. That was the artifact this description used to warn about.

fixtures.label: An account that owes nothing — the empty book
fixtures.description: The EMPTY BOOK — the only fixture that renders neither table, and the only one whose scope sentence has no sub-account clause. Address `organization:ebTofZBRYryagasD4wIX:due_date` — `organization`, NOT `-subtree`, on 20th Television / Deli Boys S2 / Office, a department with a long settled invoice history and nothing open. Re-captured 2026-09-09 on beta.386. Two jobs, and neither sibling can do either. (1) EVERYTHING IS PAID IS A REAL AND GOOD CASE. With `organizations` empty and the residual zero, the account matrix is replaced by a sentence and the detail table is dropped — the same choice `statement.eta` makes with `#no-activity`, because a headed table with no rows under it reads as a fault rather than as an answer. Without this fixture that whole arm is frozen by no golden and a green run says nothing about it, which is the failure mode templates#256 is about. (2) THE SINGULAR SCOPE. `scope.uids.length === 1`, so the scope line is the account name ALONE — no "and N sub-accounts". Its sibling `subtree-invoice-date` renders the plural arm at 14 nodes; the two are a pair and neither substitutes, because the clause is appended by a conditional that a single-node scope must not fire. ⭐ Deliberately a real settled account rather than a fabricated empty one: a report scoped to a customer who owes nothing is what someone chasing money actually runs, and a capture of it costs nothing. ⚠️ It is the smallest fixture in the family by a wide margin, which is the point — the page it freezes is a letterhead, a scope line and one sentence. ⭐ Which is why core#92 matters most HERE: that scope line used to read `Sample text for name..........`, because `applyPii` routed the stored `scope.name` to the `text` category. The field is gone and the line now composes `organization_path`, so most of this page is the fix.

fixtures.label: A bracketed credit, and an account that is only a credit
fixtures.description: HAND-BUILT, and it has to be: it carries the only shapes that exist NOWHERE in production. Measured 2026-09-08 over the whole corpus, prod holds exactly three credit notes with value left on them and all three are `void`, so `readUnappliedCredits` skips every one and no capture on any day can put a figure in the Credits column. Three jobs, none reachable otherwise. (1) THE BRACKETED CREDIT. `creditCell` brackets a non-zero credit as the deduction it is and prints a bare `$0.00` otherwise — the second arm is on every other fixture and this is the only render of the first, in both the account row and the totals footer. The zero arm exists because four rows of `( $0.00 )` read as four deductions a reader goes looking for; that was found by looking at a rendered page, and so was this. (2) A CREDITS-ONLY ACCOUNT — the second half of api-cloudrun#923. An organization holding credits and no open invoice gets its own node so the grouped rows still sum to `totals`; before that fix its money reached the footer and no row. Here it is the first line of the matrix, every bucket $0.00 and no invoice beneath it in the detail table. (3) A NEGATIVE ACCOUNT TOTAL, `-$450.00` — the only signed money cell in the family. Expect the two notations side by side rather than repairing them: Credits brackets, Total signs, and they answer different questions. ⭐ NOT typed by hand — the document is `foldAgingReport`'s own output. `organizations[]` is a SECOND derivation of `totals`, so a hand-written one could freeze a document the fold cannot produce; the receivables come from the already-masked `subtree-invoice-date` capture with one synthetic credit added, and the real fold ran. ⚠️ It never went near `applyPii` — there is no capture to run. Every masked leaf is a value the masker produced or a name from `FAKE_ORGANIZATIONS`, so `maskVerdict` settles it as it settles a capture. Keep it that way. ⭐ Also, for now, the only fixture whose two tables agree on an account's name — core#91.
